result.title: Advancement or Acceleration? How Data Curation Improves LLM Training
result.summary: While data curation is widely credited with improving large language model training, a basic question remains unresolved: does curation expand what a model can ultimately learn, or merely reach the same solution faster? In this paper, we formalize this distinction between advancement (improving the attainable performance) and acceleration (reaching the same performance with less data). Through an analytic characterization and real-world LLM experiments, we show that advancement requires a correctable train-target gap. When the baseline training and target objectives coincide, no curation policy improves the endpoint, although curation may still accelerate training. This reframes advancement as a property of the curation task rather than the curation method. Under a common gap-centric view of data mixture and selection, we operationalize this condition as the $Δ$-test, an observable discrepancy between the uncurated baseline's training and target losses that is computable prior to expensive curation. Across extensive experiments, an appreciably nonzero $Δ$ predicts persistent gains, whereas gains near $Δ=0$ tend to diminish as the training budget grows. Beyond individual methods, our findings recenter data curation on the task itself and point to target-set construction as a promising direction for shaping what curation can achieve.

AI.brief_summary: 论文将数据策展的作用形式化为「推进」（提升可达性能上限）与「加速」（以更少数据达到同样性能）的区分，通过解析刻画与真实 LLM 实验说明推进需要存在可纠正的训练—目标差距，并把这一条件操作化为可在昂贵策展前计算的 Δ-test，用其预测策展收益是否随训练预算增长而持续。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「训练—目标差距决定数据选择能否带来上限增益」的诊断，可能可供核查 LVR 轨迹训练中筛选推理轨迹或分配监督时，增益究竟来自能力扩展还是单纯收敛加速。
